Invalid chmod commands in remove_world_writable_permissions.py causing upgrade failures and configuration file corruption
Status Update:
The remove_world_writable_permissions.py script contains a issue where octal permission values are incorrectly converted to decimal in f-string formatting, causing invalid chmod commands during ERA upgrades. This leads to:
 * Failed permission setting operations

 * Configuration file corruption/deletion (including rsyslog_cfg.json)

 * System entering degraded state

 * PostgreSQL HA cluster instability

h3. Root Cause

In remove_world_writable_permissions.py line 127, octal permission values (e.g., 0o755) are converted to decimal (e.g., 493) in f-string interpolation:
 
sudo_cmd = f"\{NDB_SUDO_CMD} chmod \{permission_to_set} \{location}"
 
 
When permission_to_set = 0o755, this produces: chmod 493 /path (invalid)
